@[expose] public section

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos571

/--
Show that for any rational $\alpha \in [1,2)$ there exists a bipartite graph $G$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\asymp n^{\alpha}.$$

The proof constructs balanced rooted models for all rational parameters. Its upper-bound closure replaces old edges by paths
of arbitrary length, adds two color-class hubs, and commutes with positive rooted powers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/2f055a777231a73a305b379e993c37f00ed5a66b/problems/571/Erdos571.lean"]
theorem erdos_571 :
    ∀ α : ℚ, 1 ≤ α → α < 2 →
      ∃ q : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin q), G.IsBipartite ∧
        Asymptotics.IsTheta atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (α : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos571

review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos571.erdos_571, faithfully states the source page’s order-of-magnitude problem. The graph is finite and fixed independently of n, containment is ordinary (not induced) subgraph containment, and IsTheta gives exactly the required asymptotic comparison. In /workspace/review/semantics.lean, I proved equivalence with eventual positive two-sided constant bounds and checked small extremal numbers and degenerate forbidden graphs; empty graphs cannot supply spurious witnesses. The older literature also discusses stronger limiting-constant formulations, but the source page explicitly asks for Θ growth. The solved/formal_proof metadata agrees with the source. I independently compiled the unchanged cited proof using its pinned Lean 4.28.0 and Mathlib revision 8f9d9cff6bd728b17a24e163c9402775d9e6a365; compilation succeeded, and #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
